title: SLI Forecasting Simulation Runner and Initiative Splitter
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a reproducible simulation runner that ingests historical SLIs and traffic patterns to forecast error-budget runway per service and compute a suggested allocation (initiative splitter) of remaining error budget across active initiatives. Outputs will feed the Console rollout gates and the Initiative Dashboard to automate throttles and priority-adjusted rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation runner ingests at least 30 days of SLI data and produces Monte Carlo error-budget depletion curves for each service within 10% of observed burn-rate variance.
Initiative Splitter recommends fractional allocations for at least three concurrent initiatives and exposes an API endpoint used by the Console rollout policy engine.
Dashboard visualization exists showing projected runway, probability of breach, and recommended throttle percentage for each active initiative.
Automation playbook established: if probability of SLO breach > 35% within 7 days, trigger canary pause and notify on-call via PagerDuty.
End-to-end integration test covering simulated traffic replay, allocation computation, and Console API call is present in CI.
milestones: M1: Spec + data agreement with Observability (2026-03-05)
M2: Lightweight simulation prototype using BigQuery exports (2026-03-18)

M4: Canary automation + runbook and QA (2026-04-07)
M5: Public rollout and post-launch monitoring (2026-04-15)
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff with Observability and Infra. Agreed telemetry export columns and sampling window. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Reliability/SLI+Forecasting+Spec
2026-03-08: Prototype PoC shows Monte Carlo runs finish in ~25s for a single service using 30 days of QPS and latency histograms. Notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1SLI-sims
2026-03-12: Design review with Console team. Decided to expose Splitter via /api/v1/initiative_allocations to minimize coupling. Action: ENG-8421 to add auth scope.
2026-03-14: UX mockups for Initiative Dashboard accepted by PM and Design. PR with initial charts opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/987
2026-03-15: Ran preliminary end-to-end run against staging telemetry. Results flagged overfitting to weekend traffic; we will add weekday/weekend seasonal model.
decisions: Use Monte Carlo with bootstrapped trace sampling rather than parametric analytic model to better capture heavy-tail token bursts.
Expose both deterministic allocation suggestion and a confidence band so teams can choose conservative vs aggressive enforcement.
Initial gating threshold default set to 35% probability of breach in 7 days based on ops risk appetite survey.
risks: Risk of over-allocating error budget to low-priority initiatives during transient traffic spikes; mitigated by confidence bands and manual override.
Data fidelity: missing SLI labels from edge clusters could skew forecast; dependency on ENG-3304 to finish telemetry tagging.
Automated throttles may slow down business-critical feature rollouts if priority metadata is incorrect; require human-in-loop approvals for P0 initiatives.
